description: Validatable custom event catalogue for TrackFlow. Validation rules are documented in telemetry-plan.md.

privacyContract.description: The envelope userId is anonymous, system-scoped, or pseudonymous and is governed for every event. Each event flag additionally identifies sensitive or personal data in that event's properties.

eventId.description: Producer-generated UUID; consumers deduplicate on this value.

sessionId.description: Opaque random session identifier; never an auth token or cookie.

userId.description: Pseudonymous HMAC of the TinyDB user UUID, 'anonymous' before authentication, or 'system' for scheduled processes.

schemaVersion.description: Semantic version of this event's schema.

requestId.description: Correlation id propagated from browser to FastAPI and downstream events.

properties.description: Payload validated against the selected event's property allowlist.

inbound_order_created.description: A warehouse commits a goods receipt from a client.

delivery.justification: Incoming volume changes capacity and stock immediately; operations must see it within seconds.

privacy.handling: Use internal opaque ids only; never include purchase-order text, recipient, address, or auth data.

inbound_order_created.emissionControl: Emit once from the backend transaction outbox after commit; never sample.

stock_after.description: Computed warehouse stock after the committed receipt.

reference_present.description: Whether an internal receipt reference exists; never send its value.

outbound_order_created.description: A warehouse completes and commits a customer dispatch.

delivery.justification: Outbound throughput and stock availability affect the active shift and delivery SLA.

privacy.handling: Record only internal ids and tracking_present; never include tracking numbers or recipient data.

outbound_order_created.emissionControl: Emit once from the backend transaction outbox after commit; never sample.

quantity.description: Units dispatched to a customer shipment.

exit_type.description: Confirms this mandatory event represents a customer dispatch, not a loss.

stock_after.description: Computed warehouse stock after the committed exit.

tracking_present.description: Whether a dispatch has tracking; never send the tracking number.

inventory_loss_recorded.description: A warehouse commits a confirmed inventory loss through the outbound-order endpoint.

delivery.justification: Loss changes available stock immediately and may require prompt operational investigation.

privacy.handling: Use opaque client, product, and order ids; never attach free-text notes or photographs.

inventory_loss_recorded.emissionControl: Emit once from the backend transaction outbox after a loss commits; never sample.

warehouse.description: Warehouse where units were written off.

quantity.description: Units written off as a confirmed loss.

exit_type.description: Confirms this event represents a warehouse loss.

stock_after.description: Computed warehouse stock after the committed loss.

stock_threshold_triggered.description: A SKU crosses from at or above its client minimum to below it.

delivery.justification: Client and commercial alerts must arrive before a stockout blocks fulfilment.

privacy.handling: Client and product ids are opaque; do not attach client contact details.

stock_threshold_triggered.emissionControl: Emit only on the at-or-above-to-below threshold transition; re-arm when stock reaches or exceeds the threshold.

warehouse.description: Warehouse whose scoped stock crossed the threshold.

quantity.description: Current computed stock when the threshold activates.

threshold_quantity.description: Configured client minimum for this SKU.

previous_quantity.description: Stock immediately before the triggering movement.

direct_stock_edit_rejected.description: The API rejects an attempt to set or adjust stock outside an order.

delivery.justification: Repeated bypass attempts may indicate a permissions or training problem requiring immediate attention.

privacy.handling: Attribute via pseudonymous envelope userId; discard the raw body and credentials.

direct_stock_edit_rejected.emissionControl: Never sample or debounce; one security-control event per rejected request.

warehouse.description: Warehouse the user attempted to alter.

quantity.description: Attempted stock value or delta, interpreted by attempted_operation.

endpoint_template.description: Low-cardinality route template; no raw URL or query string.

inventory_discrepancy_detected.description: A physical count differs from computed system stock.

delivery.justification: A discrepancy is a client-contract risk and must reach warehouse operations promptly.

privacy.handling: Audit, client, and product ids plus stock variance are commercially sensitive; do not include operator notes or photographs.

inventory_discrepancy_detected.emissionControl: Emit once per completed audit comparison and deduplicate by audit_id plus product_id plus warehouse.

warehouse.description: Warehouse where the physical count occurred.

detection_method.description: Audit method that detected the discrepancy.

product_created.description: An authenticated user registers a new client SKU at one warehouse.

delivery.justification: Catalogue growth informs onboarding and capacity planning, which is reviewed daily rather than within seconds.

privacy.handling: Client and product ids are commercially sensitive opaque identifiers; do not emit free-text product names.

product_created.emissionControl: Emit once after the product transaction commits; never sample.

quantity.description: Initial computed stock; always zero because stock cannot be set directly.

inventory_validation_failed.description: An inbound or outbound form fails validation after a valid SKU has been selected.

delivery.justification: Validation trends guide form and training improvements in a daily product review; no immediate action is needed.

privacy.handling: Client and product ids plus attempted quantity are commercially sensitive; send stable field/reason codes and never the rejected raw value.

inventory_validation_failed.emissionControl: Debounce identical session, form_type, field_name, reason_code, and product_id combinations for 10 seconds and increment occurrence_count.

quantity.description: Attempted unit quantity; zero when empty.

reason_code.description: Stable validation reason; no raw error text.

occurrence_count.description: Number of debounced identical failures represented by the event.

outbound_order_rejected.description: The backend rejects a known-SKU outbound order for an inventory business rule.

delivery.justification: Repeated rejected exits can block the active warehouse shift and require rapid stock or training intervention.

privacy.handling: Client/product ids and quantities are commercially sensitive; send stable reason codes and never tracking numbers or response bodies.

outbound_order_rejected.emissionControl: Emit once per rejected backend request; never sample.

audit_history_viewed.description: An authenticated operator views the read-only inventory movement history.

delivery.justification: Usage informs information architecture and audit-tool investment during weekly product reviews.

privacy.handling: Use filter enums and result count only; do not emit displayed movement rows.

audit_history_viewed.emissionControl: Emit once after a successful history load; deduplicate refreshes of the same filter for 30 seconds.

warehouse_filter.description: Warehouse filter applied to the view.

load_duration_ms.description: Time from request start until the history is usable.

login_succeeded.description: A user establishes a valid backoffice session.

delivery.justification: Successful-login volume supports adoption and staffing analysis in daily aggregates.

privacy.handling: Envelope userId is an HMAC pseudonym; never emit email, token, password, IP address, or user agent.

login_succeeded.emissionControl: Emit once per successful authentication response; never client-retry the same eventId.

session_age_seconds.description: New sessions begin at zero seconds.

login_failed.description: A login attempt fails without revealing whether an account exists.

delivery.justification: A burst can indicate credential abuse and must feed near-real-time security alerting and rate limits.

privacy.handling: Optional principal_hash is HMAC-SHA-256 of normalised email with a rotating secret; never emit raw email, password, IP, or provider error.

login_failed.emissionControl: Do not sample or client-debounce security failures; enforce API rate limiting separately and deduplicate only by eventId.

reason_code.description: Non-enumerating failure code returned to telemetry.

principal_hash.description: Rotating HMAC pseudonym for abuse correlation.

attempt_number.description: Failure count in the current server-side rate-limit window.

session_expired.description: The API rejects an otherwise well-formed request because its session token expired.

delivery.justification: Expiry patterns guide session-duration UX changes in weekly reviews; the user already receives an immediate local redirect.

privacy.handling: Use the envelope's pseudonymous userId; never emit the token, cookie, or raw URL.

session_expired.emissionControl: Emit once per sessionId; suppress subsequent 401s caused by the same expired session for 15 minutes.

session_age_seconds.description: Age of the session when rejected.

route_template.description: Sanitised route template active when expiry was detected.

authorization_denied.description: An authenticated user is denied an operation by role or ownership policy.

delivery.justification: Repeated denials may indicate permission drift or misuse requiring timely investigation.

privacy.handling: Attribute only through pseudonymous userId and low-cardinality role names; never emit resource contents.

authorization_denied.emissionControl: Emit every backend denial; aggregate alerting by userId, endpoint_template, and five-minute window.

password_reset_requested.description: The password-reset endpoint accepts or rate-limits a request without disclosing account existence.

delivery.justification: A reset-request burst may indicate account targeting and must reach abuse detection quickly.

privacy.handling: Use a rotating principal_hash only; never emit email, reset token, delivery address, or provider response.

password_reset_requested.emissionControl: Emit once per server request and retain rate limiting; never sample.

principal_hash.description: Rotating HMAC pseudonym for abuse correlation.

page_viewed.description: An authenticated user completes a backoffice route transition.

delivery.justification: Navigation popularity supports weekly information-architecture decisions, not immediate intervention.

privacy.handling: Emit route templates and section enums only; remove ids, query strings, fragments, and referrer URLs.

page_viewed.emissionControl: Emit once per completed route transition; suppress the same route_template within the same session for five seconds.

route_template.description: Low-cardinality route template with ids removed.

viewport_class.description: Coarse viewport class; no screen fingerprint.

workflow_started.description: A user begins a defined multi-step or submission workflow.

delivery.justification: Start volume becomes useful when compared with completion and abandonment in daily funnels.

privacy.handling: Use a random flow_instance_id and controlled workflow names; never capture field values.

workflow_started.emissionControl: Emit once per flow_instance_id when the first meaningful interaction occurs, not on initial render.

flow_instance_id.description: Random id joining lifecycle events for one workflow attempt.

entry_point.description: How the user entered the flow.

workflow_completed.description: A defined workflow reaches its intended successful outcome.

delivery.justification: Daily funnel conversion guides UX prioritisation and operator training.

privacy.handling: Use controlled outcomes and random flow identifiers; never include submitted form contents.

workflow_completed.emissionControl: Emit once per flow_instance_id after confirmed success; consumers deduplicate retries by eventId.

flow_instance_id.description: Random id joining lifecycle events for one workflow attempt.

duration_ms.description: Elapsed time from workflow_started to success.

workflow_abandoned.description: A started workflow has no completion within its defined timeout or ends on navigation/session expiry.

delivery.justification: Abandonment requires joining lifecycle events and informs daily funnel analysis rather than real-time operations.

privacy.handling: Derived from event ids and controlled steps; do not capture typed but unsubmitted values.

workflow_abandoned.emissionControl: Derive once in hourly processing: 30-minute timeout for forms, 10-minute timeout for freight quotes; suppress if completion later arrives inside the watermark.

api_latency_recorded.description: FastAPI middleware records a completed request's latency and result class.

delivery.justification: SLA-impacting latency and error spikes require operational detection within minutes.

privacy.handling: Use route templates and coarse status classes; omit paths, query strings, headers, bodies, IPs, and user agents.

api_latency_recorded.emissionControl: Keep 100% of errors and requests at or above the SLO; deterministically sample 10% of healthy requests by requestId.

slo_exceeded.description: Whether duration exceeded the endpoint SLO.

page_load_recorded.description: The browser records when a backoffice route becomes usable.

delivery.justification: Daily percentiles are sufficient for frontend performance prioritisation; individual slow loads do not require paging.

privacy.handling: Use route templates and coarse device classes; do not emit full URLs or browser fingerprints.

page_load_recorded.emissionControl: Emit one measurement per route transition; retain 100% of slow loads and deterministically sample 10% below the threshold.

threshold_exceeded.description: Whether the three-second usability target was exceeded.

frontend_error_captured.description: The backoffice error boundary captures an uncaught client error.

delivery.justification: A new or rapidly increasing error can block warehouse workflows and requires prompt engineering response.

privacy.handling: Generate error_code and fingerprint from a server-side scrubbed stack; never emit raw messages, stack values, DOM, form data, URL parameters, or tokens.

frontend_error_captured.emissionControl: Deduplicate the same error_fingerprint, route_template, release, and sessionId for 60 seconds; increment occurrence_count.

error_fingerprint.description: Hash of scrubbed error type and stack frames.

handled.description: Whether a local fallback prevented a full-page failure.

api_error_returned.description: FastAPI returns a controlled 4xx or 5xx response.

delivery.justification: A 5xx spike or unexpected 4xx concentration can block active operations and needs rapid triage.

privacy.handling: Emit stable error codes only; never send exception text, traceback, request/response bodies, headers, query strings, or database URLs.

api_error_returned.emissionControl: Emit all 5xx and business-rule 4xx events; aggregate identical validation 4xx events by requestId and reason code.

duration_ms.description: Server duration before the error response.

retryable.description: Whether the caller may safely retry.
